name: Knife River Corp.

events.what: Strata Corporation acquisition closed (largest deal in company history); just OUTSIDE the 18-month window (cutoff 2025-04-02)
Bolt-on acquisitions in window (five in 2025, three aggregates-based deals in early 2026 incl. Texcrete), financed by a $400M Term Loan B upsize in Q2 2026
Chief Accounting Officer appointed (internal); prior CAO moved to SVP Financial Strategy

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Level (20%) is a long-term goal with no year; the CEO declined to give timing when asked on the Q4 2025 call. The dated 2023 Investor Day step (15% by 2025) was reached. 2026 guide is a +10 to 20 bps rate, about 16% at the midpoint.

statements.quote: Combined, we expect each of the ongoing efforts in our Competitive Edge Plan will help drive consistent EBITDA growth and enable us to achieve our long-term goal of 20% Adjusted EBITDA Margin.
statements.speaker: Brian Gray
statements.doc_title: Knife River Corp. Q3 2025 Earnings Call

statements.quote: And so how do we kind of put this all together as you try to hit your 20% margin target? You know, is this, are you accelerating it, or, you know, when do we actually kind of see you achieve those levels?
statements.speaker: Ian Zaffino
statements.doc_title: Knife River Corp. Q4 2025 Earnings Call

statements.quote: And it's not linear, as you know, I mean, you pick up some lower-hanging fruits, sometimes. And so we do expect margin expansion to continue, in all of these, product lines and, you know, we're very excited about that.
statements.speaker: Brian Gray
statements.doc_title: Knife River Corp. Q4 2025 Earnings Call

statements.quote: For 2026, we expect consolidated revenue between $3.3 billion and $3.5 billion and Adjusted EBITDA between $520 million and $560 million, which implies an Adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 16% at the midpoint.
statements.speaker: Nathan Ring
statements.doc_title: Knife River Corp. Q4 2025 Earnings Call

statements.quote: Yes, our EBITDA or midpoint margin for the midpoint is going up, you know, 10-20 basis points from last year.
statements.speaker: Brian Gray
statements.doc_title: Knife River Corp. Q4 2025 Earnings Call

street.gap_assumption: No target year, so the gap uses the last consensus year (FY2028, 601.1M / 3,766.6M = 15.96%) against the 20% goal, same metric. FY2026 consensus (15.11%) sits below the guide-implied ~16% after the 2026-08-04 raise of revenue guidance with EBITDA held at $520M to $560M.

evidence_of_progress.note: Order is [Q1 2026, Q2 2026]. Q1 is a seasonal loss quarter (-7.8% vs -10.7%, consensus actuals). Q2 2026 adj. EBITDA $139.7M vs $140.8M, margin 14.9% vs 16.9% (8-K EX-99 0001628280-26-052184, doc 143103), on diesel costs, weather delays, lower-margin legacy acquired contracting jobs. TTM 6/30/26 adj. EBITDA margin 15.2% ($501.6M / $3,307.5M) vs 15.8% for FY2025 ($496.5M / $3,146.0M), both as reported in doc 223848, so the trailing margin has slipped since year end.

verdict: Numeric-framing match without a catalyst: the CEO has repeated a 20% adjusted EBITDA margin goal for three years and consensus sits about 400 bps short, but there is no leadership change, Strata closed just outside the window, the goal has no date, and margins went backwards in Q2 2026.
open_questions: Will management attach a year to the 20% goal, or quietly drop it (the 2026-09-23 investor deck lists margin improvement as a priority; no 20% figure found in the chunk read)?
How much of the Q2 2026 200 bps margin decline is diesel and legacy acquired jobs that roll off versus structurally lower-margin Mountain and Central mix?
Is pricing power on aggregates enough to offset energy inputs, or is margin more input-cost driven than the EDGE narrative implies?
